(a) cyclopentadienyl anion: 2 pi electrons from the two double bonds plus the carbanion lone pair \(= 6\) pi electrons, aromatic. (b) cyclopentadienyl cation: only 4 pi electrons, antiaromatic, hence not aromatic. (c) cyclobutadienyl dication: one double bond and two empty p orbitals \(= 2\) pi electrons \((n=0)\), aromatic. (d) cyclobutadienyl dianion: one double bond plus two carbanion lone pairs \(= 6\) pi electrons, aromatic. (e) tropylium (cycloheptatrienyl) cation: 6 pi electrons, aromatic. (f) cyclooctatetraene: 8 pi electrons and a non-planar tub shape, not aromatic. (g) cyclobutadiene: 4 pi electrons, antiaromatic, not aromatic. (h) cyclopropenyl cation: 2 pi electrons, aromatic. Aromatic set \(=\) a, c, d, e, h; not aromatic \(=\) b, f, g.

authoredSolutions.43: The figure shows \(H-C \equiv C-CH_{2}-CH(CH_{3})-CH_{3}\) with the C-H bonds labelled I (on the terminal sp carbon of the triple bond), II (the \(CH_{2}\) next to the triple bond), III (the tertiary CH) and IV (a primary \(CH_{3}\)). authoredSolutions.44: The four figures are (p) propanoyl chloride, (q) a mixed anhydride (propanoic-ethanoic anhydride), (r) ethyl propanoate and (s) propanamide. Hence the order is \(p > q > r > s\).
